models.model_label: Big 4 office size and subsequent client restatement risk, full sample (Table 4, Full sample column)
models.sample_description: Pooled U.S. client firm-years of U.S. Big 4 practice offices for fiscal years 2003–2008 under the COMPUSTAT fiscal-year convention, using Audit Analytics (fiscal years ending January 1–May 31 are labeled as the previous year). The full sample is selected to maximize N and include smaller firms excluded from COMPUSTAT. It excludes foreign filers, observations without a determinable engagement office, and observations missing industry classification, client total assets, loss, auditor, audit fees, or nonaudit fees. For restatement firms, auditor/office is identified from the auditor of record when the restated statements were originally issued. The sample has 23,190 firm-years and 2,557 subsequent restatements; the Audit Analytics restatement database is as of October 20, 2011, with fiscal years ending in 2008 to allow subsequent restatements to be observed.

sample.quote: The first sample is termed the full sample and is drawn from the period 2003–2008 from the Audit Analytics population (using the COMPUSTAT fiscal year convention).
Audit Analytics data is converted to COMPUSTAT fiscal year convention (i.e., when a company’s fiscal year ends between January 1 and May 31, the previous year is used to denote its fiscal year).

We restrict the sample to U.S. clients of U.S. Big 4 practice offices, and for restatement firms the auditor/office identification is based on the auditor of record when the restated financial statements were originally issued.

We exclude foreign filers and limit the full sample only to those observations for which we can determine the engagement office, and those observations which have the necessary (nonmissing) data for the control variables: industry classification, client size (total assets), loss (negative net income), auditor, audit fees, and nonaudit fees.
These screens result in a Big 4 client sample of 23,190 firm-year observations, of which 2,557 firm-year observations (11.1 percent of the sample) have subsequent restatements.
Accounting restatements are identified using the Audit Analytics Restatements database as of October 20, 2011.

review_notes: Selected Table 4, Full sample column as the principal H1 test. The authors say the full sample is their initial analysis to maximize sample size and avoid sample-selection bias from the COMPUSTAT/CRSP merge; the reduced expanded-controls column is secondary. Table 5 onward tests later restatement partitions or magnitude questions and is excluded.

The Table 4 continuation note explicitly states that SEC regional-office fixed effects are included in all models; this model-specific note supplies a fourth fixed-effect family beyond the three in the general Equation (1) description and the Table 4 body rows.

For the selected Table 4 model, used the table-specific definition of AUDITOR_CHANGE as a client auditor change in year t; the research-design text describes the first-year restatement exposure. Table row NON_AUDIT and note spelling NONAUDIT refer to the same fee measure.
results_review_notes: Table 4’s printed star legend and observed markers/p-values are internally inconsistent; no marker meaning is used to replace the numeric p-values. Descriptive statistics are restricted to the outcome and predictors retained in the full-sample baseline model.
